description:
sct.rs:138: `pub struct SctList(pub Vec<SignedCertificateTimestamp>);` exposes the inner Vec as public. The parser (`from_serialized_list`) carefully rejects empty lists per RFC 6962 §3.3 (`sct_list<1..2^16-1>`), but a caller writing `SctList(Vec::new())` directly produces an empty list that the type system claims is valid.

Public-surface fossilization risk: the doctest at verify.rs:144 ALREADY uses this pattern: `let sct_list = SctList(vec![]);`. The library's own example demonstrates bypassing the parser's invariant.

Maintenance consequence: callers will produce code like
  let scts = if cert_has_extension { parse(...)? } else { SctList(vec![]) };
and library invariants ('every SctList has at least one SCT') are violated. The next person to touch `SctList` will have to deal with the fact that the invariant cannot be relied on, even though the parser enforces it.

Fix options:
1. Make the inner field private. Provide `.scts() -> &[SignedCertificateTimestamp]`, `.into_inner() -> Vec<...>`, and an explicit constructor that re-validates the RFC 6962 §3.3 non-empty rule. Breaking change; pre-1.0 is the time.
2. Document that the type is just 'a Vec of SCTs with no invariants beyond the inner SCT's invariants' and remove the empty-list rejection from the parser.

Either is acceptable; the current 'parser enforces an invariant the type can't' is the worst of both worlds.
title: SctList's inner Vec is pub — callers can bypass parser invariants
